reasoning: The offer document is prepared under 2443 and is normally emailed ahead; presenting it means walking the seller through the terms and advising on a response, which is the start of negotiation. That is interpersonal persuasion and advice, not a separate checkable deliverable, so Y's single INTERPERSONAL part fits better than X's split into live and forwarded halves.

Following up with escrow, lender, inspector and pest operator is done by calls and emails, and it ends in something checkable: contingencies cleared and the deal ready to close. Y's DISCRETE coding captures that, whereas X treats it as pure interaction with no output.

X codes at the level of handover: one property's ads and MLS entry go live as a package, and one open house is a single hosted event. Y's per-visitor open-house unit and its separate ad and MLS items are finer than how the work is handed over.

Even when a buyer asks for a showing live, the agent has to confirm the time with the listing agent or seller (often through a showing service or text) afterwards, so the appointment is completed outside the contact. One DISCRETE part, as in Y, fits better than a 50/50 live split.

A showing is a client-facing service encounter with a natural unit, one property shown to a client, and the client is present throughout. LIVE_SERVICE with that work item fits better than INTERPERSONAL, and it matches the treatment of 2455 and 2452.

Going through construction plans and recommending options is a service consultation with the client present and has a clear unit, one plan review. LIVE_SERVICE is consistent with how showings and live advice are coded here.

Both coders split live and written answers. X keeps the statement's specific topics (construction, financing, maintenance, repairs, appraisals), and its larger written share reflects how much agents now handle by text and email. Y broadens the text to any transaction question.
Accompanying a buyer on a visit and advising on it is a client-facing service with a clear unit, one accompanied visit. LIVE_SERVICE is consistent with 2450.

Staging advice is usually given on a walk-through with the seller and often followed by a written list of fixes, so it happens in two places. Y follows Example D and codes the live consultation consistently with the other advisory statements.

Arranging a meeting between buyer and seller means coordinating both sides and their agents, which is completed afterwards by calls and messages rather than while one client waits. One DISCRETE part, as in Y, is consistent with 2448.

Advising clients on market conditions, prices and mortgages is client service delivered mostly in live conversations, with some written follow-up such as market summaries. X's live/written split matches how the other advisory statements (2453, 2456) are coded.
Reading listings and attending seminars are alternative ways of staying current, with the same purpose and the same NO_DELIVERABLE type. Splitting them, as X does, adds nothing.

An appraisal combines an on-site inspection, which is hands-on work away from the computer, with desk valuation and reporting. The instructions require splitting partly physical activities, as X does.

Soliciting rental listings is outreach to owners by phone or in person, whose value is in persuading them, while compiling listings is desk work that produces records. These are different activities, and X splits and types them correctly.

X's work item, a whole rental placement from engagement to signed lease, is a whole project, which the instructions rule out. Y breaks it into handover-level items (listing, showing, application processing, lease), and the application screening is not covered elsewhere.
